title: Conjugating a cocharacter into a prescribed maximal torus
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $(\mathbf G_m)^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^	imes$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; a maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. Let $G$ be smooth and connected, let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, and let $\mu:\mathbf G_m	o G$ be a homomorphism of $k$-group schemes, called a cocharacter. There exist $g\in G(k)$ and a cocharacter $
u:\mathbf G_m	o T$ such that $g\mu g^{-1}$ is the composite of $
u$ with $T\hookrightarrow G$. Explicitly, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $t\in A^	imes$, one has $g_A\mu_A(t)g_A^{-1}=
u_A(t)$ in $G(A)$. The trivial cocharacter and the rank-zero torus are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355 (conjugacy of maximal tori); Sections 12c--12f (the scheme-theoretic image of a cocharacter is a torus, possibly trivial).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] to $\mu:\mathbf G_m\to G$. It supplies an affine finite-type group $I$, a faithfully flat homomorphism $u:\mathbf G_m\to I$ and a closed subgroup inclusion $j:I\hookrightarrow G$ with $\mu=j\circ u$. The source $\mathbf G_m$ is a rank-one torus. Thus [lem-sfb-torus-homomorphism-image], applied to this very factorization, says that $I$ is a torus. This retains scheme-theoretic kernels, including inseparable kernels; no assertion about the image of $\mu$ on $A$-points is needed.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Definition 12.14 and following paragraph, printed p.236; Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355. The maximal-containing-torus argument is expanded using the cited dimension and torus-coordinate statements.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $\kundim G$ is finite. For any torus subgroup $R\subseteq G$, its split presentation identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}k[\mathbf Z^r]$ by the unconditional coordinate assertion of [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action]. The domain assertion of [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with $K=k$ makes this coordinate ring an integral domain, also for $r=0$. In particular $R$ is reduced and irreducible: the zero ideal is prime and its closure is the entire spectrum. Its dimension is a nonnegative integer. From the strict-chain definition [def-kun-dimension], every chain in the closed subset $|R|$ is also a chain in $|G|$, so $0\leq\kundim R\leq\kundim G$.

source.place: Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Definition 12.14 and following paragraph, printed p.236; Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355. The maximal-containing-torus argument is expanded using the cited dimension and torus-coordinate statements.

proof.text: Among all torus subgroups containing $I$, choose $S$ of greatest dimension; the family contains $I$ and its dimensions belong to the finite integer interval in step 2. We show that $S$ is maximal among all torus subgroups of $G$. Suppose $S\subsetneq R$ for a torus $R$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the closed subgroup inclusion is given on the affine $R$ by an ideal $J$ of $k[R]$. If $|S|=|R|$, then $J$ belongs to every prime of $k[R]$, in particular the zero prime from step 2, so $J=0$ and the inclusion is an isomorphism, a contradiction. Hence $|S|$ is a proper closed subset of $|R|$. Append the irreducible set $|R|$ to a longest chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $|S|$; all its members are closed in $|R|$. By [def-kun-dimension], this gives $\kundim R\geq\kundim S+1$, contrary to the choice of $S$ because $R$ also contains $I$. Thus $S$ is a maximal torus containing $I$.

proof.text: Both $S$ and the prescribed $T$ are now maximal tori of the same smooth connected affine finite-type group $G$ over the algebraically closed field $k$. The maximal-torus clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] gives $g\in G(k)$ with $gSg^{-1}=T$ as subgroup schemes. Use the order $T_1=S$, $T_2=T$, so that the conjugation has exactly the orientation required in the item. Its stated equality holds after every commutative $k$-algebra extension.

proof.text:
Conjugation $c_g(x)=g x g^{-1}$ is a group-scheme automorphism: its morphism is obtained from multiplication, inverse and the constant section $g$, and its inverse is $c_{g^{-1}}$ by the group identities in [def-sc-group-scheme]. Step 4 therefore restricts it to an isomorphism $c_g|_S:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. Compose $u:\mathbf G_m	o I$, the inclusion $I\hookrightarrow S$ and $c_g|_S$ to obtain the group-scheme homomorphism $
u:\mathbf G_m	o T$. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $t\in A^	imes$, the equality $\mu=j u$ gives $
u_A(t)=g_A\mu_A(t)g_A^{-1}$ in $G(A)$. This is the claimed factorization as morphisms and the claimed formula on all algebras. If $\mu$ is trivial, take $g=1$ and the trivial $
u$ directly; rank-zero tori in the preceding argument cause no exception.
